I say that the reflection upon each one of them — though it be incumbent — is obligatory upon us; but the nearest of them to us, and the clearest in our view, is the trace of the manifest wisdom in the species of the human being, who is the small world, and who is the proximate cause for the existence of this world. So it is incumbent upon us to consider the human being's beginning and his coming-into-being, the composing of his parts and the structuring of his members, and the benefit conferred by each one of them, and the necessity that requires his being placed and shaped as he is. Then we should consider his welfare in each one of his traits and the powers of his soul, the light of his intellect, his substances and accidents, his hopes, and the end of his matter.

For when we stand upon what we have mentioned of the human being, much of the secret of this world becomes clear to us — for he is similar to it. Some of the philosophers have said that philosophy is *man's knowing of himself* — meaning by this the knowledge of what we have mentioned about the human matter, by which one may discern the Creator (mighty and exalted) from the trace of His wisdom in him, as in Job's saying: "And from my flesh I shall see God" (Job 19:26).

So it is fitting for us — if it be so — that we should mention, of all that we have described of the matters of the human being, a small portion from each concept that will rouse the heedless one to what he must remember always, and impel him to seek what I have not mentioned. So let him submit to his Creator on account of the magnitude of His favor to him and His beneficence toward him, and magnify his thanks to Him — as the Friend (peace be upon him) said: "I will give thanks to You, for I am awesomely set apart; wonderful are Your works, and my soul knows it well. My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, intricately wrought in the depths of the earth; Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in Your book all of them were written — days were fashioned, and not one of them" (Psalms 139:14–16).

וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית סִימַן הַחָכְמָה הַנִּרְאֶה בְּהַרְכָּבַת הָאָדָם וְחִבּוּר גּוּפוֹ וְכֹחוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ וְאוֹר הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁיִּחֵד אוֹתוֹ בּוֹ הַבּוֹרֵא וְשָׂם לוֹ בּוֹ יִתְרוֹן עַל שְׁאָר הַחַיִּים שֶׁאֵינָם מְדַבְּרִים.

וְהוּא דּוֹמֶה לָעוֹלָם הַגָּדוֹל וְנִמְשָׁל אֵלָיו בְּשָׁרָשָׁיו וִיסוֹדוֹתָיו. וְאֵלָיו רָמַז אִיּוֹב בְּאָמְרוֹ (איוב י) הֲלֹא כֶחָלָב תַּתִּיכֵנִי וְכַגְּבִנָּה תַּקְפִּיאֵנִי עוֹר וּבָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁנִי וּבַעֲצָמוֹת וְגִידִים תְּסֹכְכֵנִי חַיִּים וָחֶסֶד עָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי וּפְקֻדָּתְךָ שָׁמְרָה רוּחִי.

וְהָרְבִיעִית סִימַן הַחָכְמָה הַנִּרְאֶה בְּמִינֵי שְׁאָר הַחַיִּים מִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם. מֵהֶם הַמְעוֹפֵף וְהַשּׂוֹחֶה וְהַזּוֹחֵל וְהַהוֹלֵךְ עַל אַרְבַּע לְפִי הִתְחַלְּקוּת צוּרוֹתָם וּמִדּוֹתָם וְשִׁמּוּשָׁם וַהֲנָאָתָם וְתוֹעֲלוֹתָם בָּעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּמַּעֲנֶה שֶׁהוֹכִיחַ בּוֹ הַבּוֹרֵא אֶת אִיּוֹב כְּדֵי לְהָעִיר אוֹתוֹ (שם לח) מִי יָכִין לָעֹרֵב צֵידוֹ וְגוֹ׳ וּשְׁאָר מָה שֶׁסִּפֵּר בּוֹ מִמִּינֵי הַחַיּוֹת הַמִּדְבָּרִיּוֹת וְהַיַּמִּיּוֹת.

וְהַחֲמִישִׁית סִימָן הַחָכְמָה הַנִּרְאֶה בַּצְּמָחִים וּבַמּוֹצָאִים הַמּוּכָנִים לְתַקָּנַת הָאָדָם וְאָפְנֵי תּוֹעֲלוֹתָיו בָּהֶם עַל הִתְחַלְּקוּת טִבְעֵיהֶם וּמִזְגֵיהֶם וְכֹחוֹתָם. וּכְבָר הִזְכִּירוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים בְּסִפְרֵיהֶם מִן הָעִנְיָן כְּפִי הַשָּׂגָתָם וכמ״ש (מלכים א ד) וַיְדַבֵּר עַל הָעֵצִים מִן הָאֶרֶז אֲשֶׁר בַּלְּבָנוֹן וְעַד הָאֵזוֹב אֲשֶׁר יֹצֵא בַּקִּיר וְגוֹ׳.
